question: Investor Priti tracked the total shares in her portfolio all quarter, starting with 225 shares. Her colleague, investor Sam, held a separate portfolio with a mere dozen shares to start, but only Priti's portfolio is tracked here. A stock split doubled her tracked share count. A second split tripled it again. A small purchase added 23 more shares. A dividend reinvestment added 45 more shares. Finally, a partial sale removed 68 shares from the tracked total. How many shares did Priti's tracked portfolio hold at quarter's end?

Runner Aisha tracked the total minutes she'd trained this week, starting with 32 minutes logged Monday. Her training partner, Ben, had logged a mere half of that by Monday, but only Aisha's minutes are tracked here. A Tuesday session added 58 more minutes. A Wednesday double-session doubled her tracked total. A weekend tournament then multiplied her tracked total by 8. Finally, converting her log from minutes to a training-points system for her coach — a simple unit change — she added 68 more points to the tracked total. How many training points did Aisha's tracked total show?

A hardware store tracked the total feet of rope on its main spool, starting with 107 feet. A restock added 63 more feet. A second restock added 38 more feet. The store then converted its tracking from feet to a count of pre-cut lengths, multiplying the tracked amount by 8 lengths' worth — a simple unit change. A distributor bonus then multiplied the tracked length count by 5. A separate spool of chain, unrelated to this rope, measured 200 feet. How many pre-cut lengths did the tracked total show?

A charity marathon tracked the total miles logged by its team of runners throughout race day, starting with 140 miles already banked from early morning training laps. At sunrise, a runner dropped out, and the team's tracked count was reduced by 41 miles worth of her planned segment. By mid-morning, a relay leg added 47 more miles. By midday, another leg added 30 more miles. In the afternoon, a leg added 49 more miles. By late afternoon, another leg added 49 more miles as well. By evening, a scoring correction removed 139 miles that had been double-counted. A separate charity relay in another city, unrelated to this team, logged 500 miles that day. The team also converted its pace from minutes-per-mile into an overall hours estimate for the press release, a simple unit change unrelated to the tracked mileage. How many miles did the team's tracked total show by evening?

A dairy farm tracked the total liters of milk in its holding tank throughout the day, starting with 218 liters at dawn. During the morning milking, 140 liters were shipped out to the creamery. By midday, a cheese-making order multiplied the tank's tracked volume by 7. In the afternoon, a yogurt order multiplied it by 7 again. By evening, the milk was split evenly into 6 storage jugs, and only the first jug's volume was tracked from then on. By night, a spoilage check removed 61 liters from the tracked jug. How many liters were in the tracked jug by night?

A theater troupe tracked the total number of tickets sold for opening weekend, starting with 154 tickets sold in presale. A dozen comps were given to critics, though that number has nothing to do with the tracked ticket count. A refund batch then reduced the tracked sales by 16 tickets. A doubling of interest after a good review doubled the tracked sales. A late rush added 21 more tickets. Finally, a technical issue forced the troupe to refund 172 tickets from a cancelled show. How many tickets did the tracked total show after the cancellation refund?

Tomás tracked the total dollars in his arcade token jar, starting with 17 dollars worth of tokens. His cousin Nadia, by comparison, had a jar with a mere dozen dollars worth, but only Tomás's jar is tracked here. He spent 11 dollars worth of tokens on a claw machine. He spent another 5 dollars worth on skee-ball. A birthday bonus then multiplied his tracked token value by 6. Finally, a loyalty reward multiplied his tracked value by 5. How many dollars worth of tokens did Tomás's tracked jar hold after the loyalty reward?

A charity tracked the total dollars in its emergency fund all month, starting at 234 dollars. A morning donation added 51 dollars. A dozen thank-you cards were mailed out that day, though that number has nothing to do with the fund total. An afternoon donation added 3 more dollars. A large emergency payout then removed 213 dollars from the fund. A grant then added 66 more dollars. A bank fee removed 84 dollars. Finally, a matching challenge multiplied the tracked fund by 6. How much money was in the emergency fund at the end of the month?

A city zoo tracked its total number of visitors throughout opening day, starting with 128 visitors at the gate that morning. By midmorning, 49 more visitors arrived. By midday, 25 more came through the gate. In the afternoon, a school field trip multiplied the tracked visitor count by 8. By late afternoon, a second school's arrival doubled that count. By evening, a concert crowd tripled the tracked count once more. By closing time, a headcount correction removed 2171 visitors who had already left earlier in the day. How many visitors did the tracked count show at closing time?

A candy shop had 67 pounds of gummy bears in the bulk bin. A morning sale used up 6 pounds. A big restock added 42 more pounds. A dozen new candy jars were added to the shelf, though that number has nothing to do with the gummy bear weight. The shop then repackaged the bin into individual 8-ounce bags, multiplying the tracked count by 8 to get the total number of bags. A late delivery added 5 more bags to the tracked count. Finally, a wholesale order multiplied the tracked bag count by 8. A separate bin of sour worms, unrelated to this count, held 90 pounds. How many bags did the tracked count come to?

Shopkeeper Delacroix tracked the total dollars in his antique store's register, starting with 206 dollars at opening on Monday. His partner, Ms. Fontaine, tracked the register at their second location, which opened with 900 dollars, but only this store's register is tracked here. During the morning, a customer's purchase added 27 dollars. By midday, a large estate-sale haul tripled the tracked register total. In the afternoon, a big antique clock sale required giving 370 dollars in change from the register, reducing the tracked total. By evening, a small sale added 10 more dollars. Converting the day's total from dollars to francs for an old ledger tradition — a simple unit change — the shopkeeper then subtracted a 28-dollar bank fee from the tracked total. How many dollars were in the register by the end of the evening?

A woodworking shop tracked the total number of chairs completed this month, starting with 57 chairs finished in the first week. By the second week, 72 more chairs were completed. By the third week, 14 more were finished. By the fourth week, a new automated finishing line multiplied the tracked chair count by 8. A dozen new tools were purchased for the shop that month, though that number has nothing to do with the chair count. By the final week, a rush order added 59 more chairs. Finally, a bulk export contract multiplied the tracked total by 7. How many chairs did the tracked total show by the end of the month?

Baker Simone tracked the total loaves of bread baked for the farmers market, starting with 143 loaves from the first oven batch. Her rival baker, Théo, had baked a mere dozen loaves by comparison, but only Simone's tracked loaves matter here. A second batch added 5 more loaves. A third batch added 71 more loaves. A fourth batch added 68 more loaves. A fifth batch added 23 more loaves. A separate stall selling pastries, unrelated to this count, had 200 items. Finally, a wholesale contract multiplied the tracked loaf count by 5. How many loaves did Simone's tracked total come to?

Rancher Delgado tracked the total number of cattle in the north pasture all year, starting with 162 head in early spring. His neighbor, rancher Voss, ran a herd of 900 head in a separate pasture, but only Delgado's north pasture is tracked here. By late spring, the herd was split evenly into 3 grazing rotations, and only the first rotation's count was tracked. By early summer, a new calving season added 33 more head to the tracked rotation. By midsummer, a breeding program multiplied the tracked count by 6. By late summer, a purchase added 68 more head. By fall, another purchase added 75 more head. By winter, a sale to a neighboring ranch removed 624 head from the tracked rotation. How many cattle were in the tracked rotation by winter?

Nurse Whitfield tracked the total number of bandages in Supply Cart A, starting with 131 bandages. Her colleague, nurse Boone, restocked Supply Cart B with a mere dozen bandages by comparison, but only Cart A is tracked here. A busy morning used up 40 bandages from Cart A. A bulk delivery then tripled the tracked cart's remaining bandages. An afternoon restock added 68 more bandages. A mass casualty drill used up 215 bandages from the tracked cart. Finally, an evening shift used 66 more. How many bandages were left in Cart A's tracked count?

A beekeeper tracked the total pounds of honey in the extraction barrel throughout harvest day, starting with 65 pounds at dawn. During the morning extraction, 30 pounds were bottled and removed from the barrel's tracked total. By midday, a second hive's harvest added 47 more pounds. In the afternoon, a third hive added 32 more pounds. By evening, a fourth hive added 26 more pounds. Converting the barrel's tracked weight into a jar-count estimate for the farmers market — a simple unit change — the beekeeper multiplied the tracked total by 8. A separate barrel from a neighboring apiary, unrelated to this one, held 200 pounds. How many jars did the tracked estimate come to by evening?

A community garden tracked the total number of tomatoes harvested all day, starting with 96 tomatoes picked before dawn. By early morning, a bumper crop multiplied the tracked harvest by 7. By midmorning, a second row added 41 more tomatoes. By midday, a third row added 29 more tomatoes. By afternoon, volunteers tripled the tracked harvest by picking three more rows just like the first. By evening, a late pick added 53 more tomatoes. By night, a final gathering added 74 more tomatoes. A dozen volunteers worked the garden that day, though that number has nothing to do with the tomato count. How many tomatoes did the tracked harvest show by night?

A bakery had 89 cupcakes ready for a wedding order. Each cupcake was then paired with 4 matching mini cupcakes, multiplying the tracked total. A second order multiplied that tracked count by 5. A late addition added 32 more to the tracked count. A separate order for a birthday party, unrelated to this wedding order, needed 60 cupcakes. Finally, the cupcakes were boxed evenly into 4 boxes, and only the first box's count was tracked. How many cupcakes were in the tracked box?

A shipping company tracked the total number of packages in Container A all week, starting with 216 packages. A supplier's shipment tripled the tracked package count. A regional hub then multiplied the tracked count by 6. A holiday surge multiplied it by 9 more. Converting the tracked count from packages to a weight estimate in kilograms for customs — a simple unit change — the company then subtracted 34821 units after a customs adjustment. A dozen customs agents processed the shipment, though that number has nothing to do with the tracked count. How many units did the tracked customs total show?

A blood bank tracked the total units of plasma in cold storage, starting with 221 units at dawn. During the morning, 7 more units came in from a donor drive. By midday, 21 more units arrived. A dozen refrigerators hummed in the storage room, though that number has nothing to do with the unit count. In the afternoon, a hospital transfer removed 194 units. By evening, a final donation added 64 more units. How many units of plasma were in cold storage by evening?

Rina tracked the total dollars in her craft business's earnings jar, starting with 85 dollars. Her business partner, Jules, kept a separate jar for supplies that held 500 dollars, but only Rina's earnings jar is tracked here. A big craft fair multiplied her tracked earnings by 8. A late sale added 23 more dollars. A doubling promotion then doubled her tracked total. A tip jar contribution added 3 more dollars. Converting her earnings from dollars to a loyalty-points system for regular customers — a simple unit change — she added 39 more points to her tracked total. How many points did Rina's tracked total show?

Trader Voss tracked the total number of coins in his rare-coin portfolio, starting with 100 coins. His rival, trader Petrov, held a portfolio of 900 coins, but only Voss's portfolio is tracked here. An auction win multiplied his tracked coin count by 5. A small purchase added 42 more coins. A sale then removed 64 coins. A bigger sale removed 322 more coins. A trade added 66 coins back. Finally, a bulk acquisition multiplied his tracked total by 7. How many coins were in Voss's tracked portfolio?

Grower Petra tracked the total pounds of strawberries picked in her field all morning, starting with 27 pounds picked at sunrise. Her farmhand, Solomon, was picking blueberries separately, having gathered 90 pounds, but only Petra's strawberries are tracked here. By mid-morning, a bumper row multiplied her tracked pounds by 7. By midday, a spoiled batch meant 104 pounds had to be discarded from the tracked total. In the afternoon, a second field added 72 more pounds. Converting her tally from pounds to crates for market delivery — a simple unit change — she then set aside 156 crates' worth for a separate order, subtracting it from her tracked total. How many crates were in Petra's tracked total by the end of the afternoon?

A ski resort tracked the total inches of snow on its main slope throughout the storm, starting with 44 inches at dawn. During the morning, 41 inches melted off under a warm patch before more snow came. By midday, a fresh burst added 56 more inches. In the afternoon, another burst added 42 more inches. By evening, a third burst added 36 more inches. By night, a final burst added 69 more inches. How many inches of snow were on the slope by night?

Referee Doyle tracked the total penalty minutes assessed in a hockey game, starting with 20 minutes from the first period. His fellow referee, Marsh, tracked penalty minutes in a different rink's game, which totaled 90 minutes, but only Doyle's game is tracked here. During the second period, 69 more minutes were assessed. During the third period, another 69 minutes were assessed. In overtime, a review overturned 117 minutes' worth of calls, removing them from the tracked total. Finally, a post-game review added 30 more minutes. How many penalty minutes did Doyle's tracked game show after the review?
